outcome: No event since 26 January 2024 settles or moves Newman's conjecture for any modulus; the only in-window item bearing on it is the journal publication (Advances in Mathematics, September 2025) of Choi and Lee's density-1 result, whose first posting is dated December 2022, and the conjecture is still listed as unsolved on Wikipedia as of 2026.
problem_asks: (1) For every positive integer M (the modulus). (2) For every residue r modulo M (Wikipedia: every integer r with 0 <= r <= M-1; Choi and Lee: 'for each integer r'). (3) That the ordinary partition function p(n) satisfies p(n) = r (mod M) for infinitely many non-negative integers n. This is one universal claim quantified over all moduli and all residues, not a claim about a single modulus. The frozen wording is 'the partition function satisfies any arbitrary congruence infinitely often', which is the same content. Not asked by this bullet: the weaker existence statement that p(n) = 0 (mod m) has at least one solution (the Erdos-Ivic/Erdos question, which Schinzel settled for the infinitude version).

events.what_happened: Morris Newman, 'Periodicity modulo m and divisibility properties of the partition function', Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 97 (1960) 225-236. Newman formulated the conjecture in 1960 (Wikipedia infobox gives 25 March 1960 as the conjecture date). Per Wikipedia's known-cases summary, the paper proves the case m = 5 and m = 13. Choi and Lee's list gives Newman as one of the attributions for M = 2, 5 and 13.
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia's known-cases summary: the conjecture for m = 5 and m = 13. The full text was not readable, so the exact scope of the paper is not verified.
events.remains: Every other modulus, including composite moduli and modulus 3.
events.time_since_posted: 66 years; later papers (Ono 2000, Ahlgren 2000, Ahlgren-Boylan 2003 and 2005, Choi-Lee 2022) cite and build on it. No separate verification of the 1960 paper was found.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture: establishes instances (m = 5, 13) and states the general claim.

events.what_happened: Oddmund Kolberg (1959), per Wikipedia and Choi-Lee's citation list: the partition function takes both even and odd values infinitely often, i.e. the case m = 2. Choi and Lee's v2 summary credits Kolberg with M = 2. The original paper was not opened.
events.delivers: The conjecture for m = 2 (parity of p(n) takes both values infinitely often).
events.direction: Supports the conjecture (m = 2 instance).

events.what_happened: Morris Newman, Illinois J. Math. 6(1) (1962). Per Wikipedia's known-cases summary this paper proves the case m = 65. A search excerpt also credits Newman (1962) with an independent proof of the parity result (m = 2). Neither the paper nor an abstract was opened.
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia: the case m = 65 (composite, coprime to 6, and later covered by Ahlgren 2000). Per a search excerpt: the parity case (m = 2).
events.doubts: The m = 65 attribution is from Wikipedia's summary and the paper was not read; the 1962 attribution of the parity result is from a search excerpt. Both unverified.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture (instances).

events.what_happened: Small-modulus instances credited in Choi-Lee's v2 introduction (opened via arXiv HTML): Atkin and Kloeve for M = 7; Kloeve for M = 17, 19, 29 and 31. The Kloeve reference is Mathematica Scandinavica 1968 (per a search excerpt, not opened). A search excerpt also credits Atkin, Newman and Kolberg with M = 2, 5, 7, 11, 13; that list includes 11 and Choi-Lee's list does not. The dates of the individual results are not established.
events.delivers: The conjecture for M = 7, 17, 19, 29, 31 (per Choi-Lee's citation). Whether M = 11 is covered is in conflict between sources.
events.time_since_posted: about 58 years (date of the Kloeve reference; the M = 7 result is undated)
events.doubts: The 1968 date belongs to the Kloeve reference only; the M = 7 result may be earlier. The M = 11 status conflicts between sources and was not resolved.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture (instances).

events.what_happened: Ken Ono, 'Distribution of the partition function modulo m', Ann. of Math. (2) 151 (2000) 293-307. arXiv math/0008140, a single version submitted 17 Aug 2000. The abstract (opened) states there are infinitely many partition congruences for every prime modulus exceeding 3, and gives a simple criterion guaranteeing Newman's conjecture for any prime modulus exceeding 3. Per Choi-Lee (opened) and Wikipedia: a prime m >= 5 is 'good' if for every residue r there is n_r >= 0 with m n_r = -1 (mod 24) and p((m n_r + 1)/24) = r (mod m); a good prime m gives Newman for m; a computation verifies Newman for every prime m < 1000 except m = 3.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (17 Aug 2000). Journal version Ann. of Math. 151(1), 2000.
events.delivers: Newman's conjecture for every prime m >= 5 that satisfies the good-prime criterion; per Wikipedia and Choi-Lee, the computational verification for every prime m < 1000 except possibly 3. The criterion is a sufficient condition, not a proof for all primes.
events.remains: Modulus 3 (excluded by the paper's own computation); every composite modulus, except what Ahlgren 2000 added; powers of 2 and 3; primes >= 1000 unless the criterion holds for them (Ono's paper notes it appears likely every prime >= 13 is good but that proving this needs substantial computation, per a search excerpt, not verified in the text).

events.what_happened: Scott Ahlgren, 'Distribution of the partition function modulo composite integers M', Math. Ann. 318 (2000), no. 4, 795-803 (MR 1802511; DOI 10.1007/s002080000142). Per Wikipedia's summary, this extends Ono's condition to all composite M coprime to 6. The paper itself was not readable; the bibliographic details come from search excerpts and Choi-Lee's reference list (opened).
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia: Newman's conjecture for all composite moduli coprime to 6 (not verified in the text).
events.remains: Prime moduli and composite moduli divisible by 2 or 3, and the other open cases of Ono 2000 and Ahlgren-Boylan.

events.what_happened: Scott Ahlgren and Matthew Boylan, 'Arithmetic properties of the partition function', Invent. Math. 153 (2003) 487-502. The main result, per secondary sources (a 2004 talk abstract, a 2022 paper and Wikipedia), is that the Ramanujan-type congruences p(l n + beta) = 0 (mod l) occur only for l = 5, 7, 11. Per Wikipedia and Choi-Lee (both opened as summaries), the paper also proves Newman's conjecture for every prime modulus l >= 5 (Wikipedia: 'all primes except possibly 3'). The paper itself was not readable.
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia and Choi-Lee: Newman's conjecture for every prime modulus l >= 5. The main Ramanujan-type result is a different question (congruences of the form p(l n + beta) = 0 mod l) and is not Newman's question.
events.remains: Modulus 3 (Wikipedia: the prime case is open 'except possibly 3'); powers of 2 and 3; composite moduli not covered by Ahlgren 2000.

events.direction: Supports the conjecture for every prime modulus l >= 5 (per secondary sources); not a settlement of modulus 3 or of composite moduli.

Ann. 331 (2005) 219-239 (bibliographic record from a search excerpt; Choi-Lee's reference list gives a second Ahlgren-Boylan paper, opened). Per Wikipedia's summary and Choi-Lee's v2 text, this proves Newman's conjecture for every prime power l^j with l >= 5.
events.delivers: Newman's conjecture for prime powers l^j with l >= 5 (per Wikipedia and Choi-Lee). Powers of 2 and 3 are not covered (Wikipedia: 'all prime powers except powers of 2 or 3').
events.remains: Powers of 2 and 3 (modulus 3 included); composite moduli with factors 2 or 3 outside the small known list (Wikipedia lists 16, 40, 65 as further known cases).

events.what_happened: Jim L. Brown and Yingkun Li, 'Distribution of powers of the partition function modulo l^j', J. Number Theory 129(10) (2009) 2557-2568 (published October 2009). The abstract (opened via the Caltech record) studies Newman's conjecture for powers of the partition function, i.e. the r-th power p_r(n) of the generating function (counting r-colored partitions), not p(n) itself. It states the conjecture is known for prime powers of primes l that are not exceptional for the power in question and is open for exceptional primes; it settles many cases for small powers by generalising Ono and Ahlgren.
events.delivers: Newman-type distribution for small powers p_r(n) of the partition generating function, in many cases; the case r = 1 (the ordinary p(n)) is not what this paper settles. Case-by-case method; no general method.
events.remains: For the question asked here: the ordinary p(n) question is not the paper's object. For the analogue: the exceptional primes for each power, per the abstract.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, J. Number Theory 129(10) (2009).

events.direction: An analogue (powers of the generating function, not p(n)) for which the abstract states the conjecture is open for exceptional primes; it does not change the status of p(n) itself.

events.what_happened: Timothy Kilbourn, AMS meeting abstract 'The distribution of powers of the partition function modulo l^j' (2006, per a search excerpt). It announces an analogue of Newman's conjecture for powers of the generating function for p(n), with a proof using methods of Serre and Swinnerton-Dyer. The AMS abstract PDF returned HTTP 403 and was not read; the full paper was not found.
events.delivers: Per the announcement: an analogue for powers of the generating function (not p(n)). No full argument found.
events.remains: The ordinary p(n) question and the analogue as stated in the excerpt.

events.what_happened: Dohoon Choi and Youngmin Lee, first posted on arXiv 1 Dec 2022 as 'Newman's conjecture for the partition function modulo odd integers' (arXiv 2212.00636 v1). The v1 abstract (opened) states: for each positive integer d, let B_d be the set of positive integers M with d prime divisors; the density of the set of M in B_d for which Newman's conjecture holds is 1. It also studies an analogue for weakly holomorphic modular forms on Gamma_0(N) with nebentypus, applied to t-core partitions and generalized Frobenius partitions with h-colours. v2 (29 May 2025) is retitled 'Newman's conjecture for the partition function modulo integers with at least two distinct prime divisors'. Published: Adv. Math. 477 (2025), article 110367 (Sept 2025, per the Korea University repository record and a ScienceDirect listing; the ScienceDirect page returned HTTP 403).
events.revisions: v1 1 Dec 2022 (title: 'modulo odd integers'); v2 29 May 2025 (title: 'modulo integers with at least two distinct prime divisors'); journal Adv. Math. 477 (2025) 110367, Sept 2025. The v1 abstract covers all M with d prime divisors, so the odd-integer title and the abstract did not agree in v1.
events.delivers: For each d >= 1, Newman's conjecture holds for a set of moduli M with exactly d prime divisors of density 1 within B_d. This is a density statement over moduli. It does not establish the conjecture for any particular modulus. Since B_1 contains all prime powers, the statement covers almost all prime powers, but not each power of 2 or 3 individually.
events.remains: Every individual modulus not in a density-1 exceptional set is not decided by this result; in particular modulus 3, and the individual powers of 2 and 3, are not settled by the density statement itself. The Newman conjecture for all M is not settled.

This seems to conflict with a density-1 statement within B_d, which implies infinitely many such M. The second half of the HTML (100k onward) did not contain it. Unresolved: it may be an extraction artefact, or may refer to a narrower claim. events.what_happened: Cristian-Silviu Radu, 'Proof of a conjecture by Ahlgren and Ono on the non-existence of certain partition congruences', Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 365 (2013) 4881-4894. The AMS abstract (search excerpt; page not opened) concerns a congruence modulo a prime l >= 5 on an arithmetic progression An + B: it forces l | A, and a Legendre symbol condition on (24B - 1)/l. Search excerpts date a preprint to 2010. A separate excerpt attributes to Radu's 2010 work the proof of the Ahlgren-Ono conjecture that every arithmetic progression contains infinitely many N with p(N) not = 0 (mod 3).
events.revisions: Journal version Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 365 (2013), 4881-4894.
events.delivers: Per the TAMS abstract excerpt: non-existence of certain congruences for primes l >= 5 on arithmetic progressions. Per the Smith-Ye excerpt: the Ahlgren-Ono statement that every progression contains infinitely many N with p(N) not = 0 (mod 3). These two descriptions do not obviously match, and the TAMS paper's own scope as excerpted concerns l >= 5.
events.remains: Newman's question for modulus 3 asks whether p(n) = 0 (mod 3) infinitely often; the Ahlgren-Ono statement concerns the non-zero residues on progressions, so on the excerpt it does not directly settle residue 0 mod 3. Unresolved.
events.time_since_posted: about 16 years; cited in later work on partition congruences (search excerpts).
events.doubts: The sources conflict on whether Radu's result covers the mod-3 Ahlgren-Ono statement at all (Smith-Ye excerpt says yes, 2010; the TAMS 2013 abstract excerpt concerns l >= 5). Neither the 2010 preprint nor the TAMS full text was read.
events.direction: Concerns a neighbouring question (congruences on progressions, and the Ahlgren-Ono mod-3 statement). Does not change the Newman status of any modulus on the sources read.

events.what_happened: Geoffrey D. Smith and Lynnelle Ye, 'An explicit approach to the Ahlgren-Ono conjecture', arXiv 1407.7285 (first version July 2014). Per the search excerpt of its abstract: a simpler proof of the Ahlgren-Ono conjecture (every arithmetic progression contains infinitely many N with p(N) not divisible by 3) in the special case where the modulus is a power of 3. The full text was not read.
events.delivers: Per the excerpt: the Ahlgren-Ono statement for progressions with power-of-3 modulus; a new proof of a result attributed to Radu.
events.remains: Not a result on Newman's conjecture; the progression statement is about values not divisible by 3.
events.direction: Concerns a neighbouring statement (the Ahlgren-Ono congruence question); does not decide Newman for modulus 3, which needs residue 0 attained infinitely often.

events.what_happened: Neil Calkin and coauthors, 'Computing the integer partition function', Math. Comp. 76 (2007) 259 (AMS record S0025-5718-07-01966-7). Per search excerpts only, not opened (the AMS page returned HTTP 403 and the Clemson-hosted PDF failed a certificate check): a computation of the residue distribution of p(N) for N up to 10^9, covering primes up to 103 and small powers of 2 and 3. The exact statement was not verified.
events.delivers: Per the excerpt: numerical evidence of the residue distribution for N <= 10^9 and listed moduli. A finite computation of instances.
events.remains: Every infinite claim: a check up to 10^9 does not settle the infinitude of n for any modulus.
events.doubts: Not opened; the coverage described comes from a search excerpt and may be wrong in detail.
events.direction: Instances only; consistent with the conjecture; decides no modulus.

Math. 490 (2026), article 110840; not verified.

events.time_since_posted: about 1 year 6 months; no engagement found

events.what_happened: Ken Ono (sole author), 'The partition function and elliptic curves', arXiv 2508.09608 (v1 13 Aug 2025; v2 16 Aug 2025; v3 3 Sep 2025; v4 6 Jul 2026). The abstract (opened) reinterprets the Bruinier-Ono trace formula for p(n) via CM points on X_0(6) and supersingular traces, for primes l >= 5 nonsplit in Q(sqrt(1 - 24n)), with applications to Ramanujan's congruences modulo powers of 5, 7 and 11. The abstract states: 'The two new algebraic identities at the heart of this framework, as opposed to the classical results it builds on, were formalized and verified in Lean by AxiomProver.'
events.revisions: v2 16 Aug 2025; v3 3 Sep 2025; v4 6 Jul 2026 (latest per the arXiv page).
events.delivers: A moduli-theoretic framework for Ramanujan's congruences (moduli 5, 7, 11). Not about residue classes of p(n) hit infinitely often; not about Newman's conjecture.
events.time_since_posted: about 14 months; no review or citing work found
events.direction: Different question; no bearing on the Newman status of any modulus on the sources read.

events.what_happened: Ken Ono and Ashvin Swaminathan (appendix by Q.-Y. Zheng), 'Parity of the partition function in quadratic progressions', arXiv 2509.09553 (v1 11 Sep 2025; v2 2 Oct 2025; v3 12 Aug 2026; v4 1 Sep 2026). The abstract (opened) proves a conjecture of Ono (2010): for square-free D = 23 mod 24, the values p((Dm^2+1)/24) with (m,6)=1 include infinitely many even and infinitely many odd terms. It gives the lower bound #{0 <= n <= X: p(n) odd} >> sqrt(X), stated as the best known lower bound for odd values of p(n). The abstract says the identities at the heart of the paper 'have been formalized in Lean by AxiomProver'.
events.delivers: Both parities of p(n) occur infinitely often along the quadratic progressions (Dm^2+1)/24 for square-free D = 23 mod 24; a positive-density-type lower bound on odd values of p(n). This is a parity result on a restricted progression.
events.remains: Newman's conjecture for modulus 2 was already known (Kolberg 1959, Newman 1962); the progression restriction means this is not a general statement for p(n) mod 2. Nothing here addresses moduli 3 or higher.
events.time_since_posted: about 13 months; no review or citing work found
events.direction: A stronger-form or restricted question for the mod-2 case; not Newman's question for any modulus as stated.

events.what_happened: M. P. Thejitha and S. N. Fathima, 'Arithmetic Properties of Partitions with 1-colored Even Parts and r-colored Odd Parts', arXiv 2509.24324 (v1 29 Sep 2025; v2 18 Nov 2025). The abstract (opened) proves infinite families of congruences modulo 3 and 5 for a_r(n), a Hirschhorn-Sellers partition function, 'by employing a result of Newman and theory of modular forms'.
events.delivers: Congruences modulo 3 and 5 for a restricted partition function a_r(n); it uses an unnamed 'result of Newman', which is not Newman's conjecture as far as the abstract shows.
events.direction: A different function and a different congruence question; neither supports nor contradicts Newman's conjecture.

events.what_happened: Jiyuan Li (sole author), 'A quadratic-residue dichotomy for two partition functions modulo 3', arXiv 2609.22340 (single version, submitted 16 Sep 2026). The abstract (opened) concerns two restricted partition functions f_{0,1,4}(n) and f_{0,2,3}(n) (parts congruent to 0, 1, 4 or 0, 2, 3 mod 5, each part used at most twice). It proves that for each prime p = 3 mod 4 there are explicit a(p), b(p) such that f_{0,1,4}(p^2 m + a(p)) and f_{0,2,3}(p^2 m + b(p)) are congruent mod 3 to f_{0,1,4}(m) and f_{0,2,3}(m) (or interchanged), depending on whether 5 is a quadratic residue mod p. The paper does not mention p(n) or Newman's conjecture (abstract page).
events.revisions: Single version per the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Congruences mod 3 for two restricted partition functions with parts restricted mod 5, along progressions p^2 m + a(p). It concerns modulus 3 but for different functions, and says nothing about whether p(n) takes the value 0 mod 3 infinitely often.
events.remains: Newman's conjecture for p(n) at modulus 3 is not addressed.
events.time_since_posted: about 3 weeks as of 2026-10-10; no engagement found

disputes.summary: Choi-Lee v2, in the first 100k characters of the HTML, has a sentence that for M with at least two prime divisors it is not known whether infinitely many such M satisfy Newman's conjecture. This is hard to square with the density-1 result for each B_d (which implies infinitely many M). The sentence did not appear in the second half. Unresolved.

Which small moduli are settled is listed differently by sources. Choi-Lee v2: Kolberg M = 2; Newman M = 2, 5, 13; Atkin and Kloeve M = 7; Kloeve M = 17, 19, 29, 31. Wikipedia: Newman 1960 M = 5, 13; Newman 1962 M = 65. A search excerpt: Atkin, Newman, Kolberg M = 2, 5, 7, 11, 13. Another excerpt: M = 2, 5, 7, 13. Whether M = 11 is settled is not resolved.

Whether Radu's work proves the Ahlgren-Ono mod-3 statement (every progression contains infinitely many N with p(N) not = 0 mod 3). A Smith-Ye excerpt attributes it to Radu (2010), but the Radu TAMS 2013 abstract excerpt concerns primes l >= 5. A third excerpt cites a different Radu paper, 'A Proof of Subbarao's Conjecture'. Unresolved; none of the Radu full texts was read.

Wikipedia (as fetched) lists Ahlgren-Boylan 2003 as extending the result to all primes except possibly 3, and Ahlgren-Boylan 2005 as extending it to prime powers except powers of 2 or 3. Choi-Lee states the same for prime powers with l >= 5. Not a true conflict, but the 2 and 3 exceptions are based on secondary summaries.

summary: Found: no event after 26 January 2024 settles, moves, or claims a proof of Newman's conjecture for any modulus. Wikipedia (fetched) still lists the conjecture as unsolved as of 2026, and no source I could find claims otherwise. The established state of play comes from pre-window work: Kolberg 1959 and Newman 1962 for modulus 2; Newman 1960 for 5 and 13 (per Wikipedia); small moduli (7, 17, 19, 29, 31) credited to Atkin, Kloeve and Kolberg in Choi-Lee's citation list; Ono 2000 (Annals, arXiv 17 Aug 2000) for prime moduli >= 5 meeting a good-prime criterion and, by computation, for primes below 1000 except 3; Ahlgren 2000 (Math. Ann.) for composite moduli coprime to 6; Ahlgren-Boylan 2003 (Invent.) and 2005 (Math. Ann.) for primes and prime powers l^j with l >= 5. On the secondary sources, the open cases are modulus 3, the powers of 2 and 3, and composite moduli divisible by 2 or 3 outside a small listed set (Wikipedia gives 16, 40, 65). The only in-window item bearing on the bullet is Choi and Lee's density-1 result: a statement that for each d, the moduli with exactly d prime divisors for which the conjecture holds have density 1. It was first posted on 1 December 2022 (v1) and so predates the window, but its journal version (Adv. Math. 477, Sept 2025) and a retitled v2 (May 2025) fall inside it. I treat the 2022 posting as the event, per the first-argument rule. Other in-window work does not bear on the bullet: Garvan-Shomanov (Apr 2025, Atkin-O'Brien congruences mod powers of 13), Ono (Aug 2025, elliptic curves and Ramanujan's congruences mod 5, 7, 11), Ono-Swaminathan (Sept 2025, parity of p(n) along quadratic progressions, which is a restricted form of the already-known mod-2 case), Thejitha-Fathima (Sept 2025, restricted partition functions mod 3 and 5) and Li (Sept 2026, two restricted partition functions mod 3). Li is the nearest work to the open modulus 3, but it concerns different functions and does not address p(n) mod 3, and its acknowledgement crediting Anthropic Claude rests only on search excerpts, not on the authors' verbatim sentence. AI search: I found no AI system credited with any part of the Newman conjecture or its partial results (searches on AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, GPT-5, Gemini Deep Think, Erdos-problem AI trackers, and AxiomProver/Lean). The AxiomProver uses found (Ono 2025 papers, Ono-Swaminathan) are Lean formalisations of identities, which per section 5.4 are not AI contributions to the mathematics, so I did not list them in ai.systems. The Ono 2025 elliptic-curves abstract says two new algebraic identities 'were formalized and verified in Lean by AxiomProver', but says nothing about who found them; I flag that for the later pass. Close calls: (1) Choi-Lee 2022 vs 2025: first posting is 2022 and so predates the window, but a reader who dates the result by the 2025 publication would put it inside. (2) The Li AI credit is recorded, but the wording is from an excerpt, so the record flags it as unverified. (3) I did not open the full texts of Ono 2000, Ahlgren 2000, Ahlgren-Boylan 2003 and 2005, or Newman 1960 and 1962. Their scopes come from secondary summaries (Wikipedia and Choi-Lee's introduction), which I flag where they matter. Some AI-related searches returned unrelated items (AlphaEvolve, a Gemini/Erdos article, AxiomProver's Andrews-Dhar work), which I did not record as events because they do not bear on this problem.
competing_reading: (a) A reader could count the Choi-Lee result as in-window progress: its journal publication (Adv. Math., Sept 2025) falls inside the window, and the density statement moves the set of moduli known to satisfy the conjecture, which is a quantity the conjecture is about. Against this: the first public argument is dated December 2022, the rule in section 5.1 dates it there, and the density statement does not establish the conjecture for any particular modulus. (b) A reader could treat Li (Sept 2026, mod 3) as progress on the open modulus 3 and the AI-credited result on it. Against this: it is about two restricted partition functions and says nothing about p(n) mod 3 hitting 0. (c) A reader could give the 2022-2026 Ono and Ono-Swaminathan results more weight as Newman-adjacent progress; but they concern elliptic-curve traces and parity along quadratic progressions, and the mod-2 case was already settled.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The verbatim acknowledgement sentence of arXiv 2609.22340 (Li), from a readable PDF or the TeX source, to confirm the Claude attribution and its wording. (2) Full texts of Ono 2000 and Ahlgren-Boylan 2003 and 2005 to confirm the exact moduli each proves, in particular whether the 2003 paper covers prime 3 and the 2005 paper covers no power of 2 or 3. (3) The final section of Choi-Lee v2, to settle the 'not known whether infinitely many M' sentence, and any zbMATH or MathSciNet review of Adv. Math. 477 (2025). (4) A zbMATH or Google Scholar cited-by list for Choi-Lee and Ono 2000 filtered to 2024-2026, to find any post-2024 work using these results. (5) The text of Radu's 2010 preprint and TAMS 2013 paper, to fix whether the mod-3 Ahlgren-Ono statement is covered. (6) The Calkin et al. 2007 paper, to confirm the computed range and moduli.

events.ai_basis: NOT VERBATIM. Paraphrase from a search-tool excerpt of the acknowledgements: 'the original pair of partition functions was suggested by an AI language model (Anthropic Claude)'.

judgement.why: The statement is a universal claim over all moduli and residues, so each pre-2024 settled class of moduli (m=2, 5, 13, 7, 17-31, primes >=5, composites coprime to 6, prime powers l^j with l>=5) is a case, digested via journals of record. Choi-Lee's density-1 result settles no individual modulus; it is a proportion over moduli, so bound, and dated to its December 2022 first posting (v2 retitling and the 2025 journal version are not new events on the record). Calkin et al. is a finite computation (instances). Brown-Li, Kilbourn, Radu, Smith-Ye and all post-snapshot items concern different functions, different congruence families, or restricted progressions for the already-known mod-2 case, so variant (Ono 2025 elliptic curves is none: it doesn't touch the question). AxiomProver only formalised identities, so none. Li 2026 credits Claude with suggesting the functions and generalising a theorem, which reads as assisted, but the event is a variant and is discarded regardless.
judgement.doubts: Li's AI credit rests on a non-verbatim search excerpt. Scopes of the pre-2024 papers come from secondary summaries; m=11 attribution conflicts. Pre-snapshot papers marked digested on journal publication alone.
